title: iOS exporter silently fails if targeted_device is wrongly set in export_presets.cfg; results in legacy window behavior
body:
### Tested versions

4.7.1.stable

### System information

macOS 15 (Apple Silicon), Xcode 26 (SDK iphoneos26.5), iPad Air (M3) on iPadOS 26.5

### Issue description

(Refiling #[122262](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/122262) using template and by hand, with apologies. Newbie mistake.)

If `application/targeted_device_family` in `export_presets.cfg` holds an out-of-range value, the iOS exporter silently emits `TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "";` in the generated Xcode project — the switch in `platform/ios/export/export_plugin.cpp` (`_process_config_file_line`) handles only 0/1/2 with no default.

The built ipa then has no `UIDeviceFamily` key, so iPadOS 26 treats the app as a legacy iPhone app and launches it in a small, non-resizable compatibility window (dead maximize button, `UIScreen.main.bounds` = 320×480). Nothing in the export output points back to the preset value. Verified on device, including a control test of identical minimal apps with and without `UIDeviceFamily`.

To comment added in my prior report: Yes, the editor's dropdown can't produce an invalid value. Arguably makes this a trivial issue. But I'd think this file is routinely modified outside the editor — scripts, CI, VCS merges, and Godot 3.x habits (where `3` was the bitmask for iPhone+iPad, which is exactly how mine got there). The export succeeds with no warning either way.

If "bug" isn't the right label, happy to post elsewhere or delete.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In any project's `export_presets.cfg`, set `application/targeted_device_family=3` in the iOS preset.
2. Export for iOS — succeeds with no warning.
3. Inspect the generated `project.pbxproj`: `TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "";`. Inspect the ipa's Info.plist: no `UIDeviceFamily`.
4. Install on an iPad with iPadOS 26: app launches in a scaled iPhone-compatibility window.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Any empty project reproduces it via step 1 — the defect is in preset handling, not project content.
